title: Normalized integral open tensor and reduction comparison data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, with the pinned coefficient and operation presentation $o$ of [def-sf-integral-open-operations]. Write $B_W$ for the completed coefficient sheaf and $A_{n+1}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1}$ for the positive finite coefficients. Use the strict quotient-system module categories and their evaluations [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], the exact derived adjunction construction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], and fixed normalized reduction calculi $S_X,S_U$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. Define finite extension and restriction by the finite coefficient equivalence followed by localized extension, respectively localized restriction followed by its inverse. Define whole-system extension and restriction by the corresponding whole-system equivalence and localized system functors; their adjunction is the composite of the equivalence adjunction with localized open adjunction. Define $J,P$ and their adjunction by termwise localization. The extension/evaluation comparison is the associator composite of the system transport evaluation and localized extension evaluation. Integral and finite extension sections are the actual direct-sum generators followed by the sheafification unit and the prescribed coefficient transport.

A tensor comparison datum consists of natural isomorphisms $e_!(-)\otimes_{B_X}A_{n+1}\cong j_!^{A_{n+1}}(-\otimes_{B_U}A_{n+1})$, for every $n\in\mathbf N$, whose maps send the scalar-unit image of every integral extension generator to the finite extension generator of its scalar-unit image. Completeness means the recorded augmented quotient-tower completeness predicate [def-weil-derived-complete].

For a complex $Q$, a strict quotient-system complex $C$, an isomorphism $e:S_W\operatorname{red}(Q)\cong C$ in the derived category, and termwise finite evaluation isomorphisms $\kappa_n$, define an augmented presentation to mean that there exists ONE chain augmentation from the constant tower of $Q$ to the scalar-restriction tower of $C$, whose sections are $\kappa_n^{-1}(x\otimes1)$ in every degree, and whose transpose under the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models] equals the transpose of $e$ under the reduction/limit adjunction. The finite reductions and scalar units are those of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower].

In functor words below composition is written left-to-right. For a proposed $r:j_!\operatorname{red}_X\cong\operatorname{red}_U J$ on complete inputs, define its strict-model predicate as follows. For EVERY complete flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], there are a K-flatness witness for its extended complex, strict-system complexes $C,D$ computing reduction of $Q,e_!Q$, their derived reduction and finite evaluation isomorphisms, and one chain isomorphism $f:D\cong JC$. Both computations satisfy the reduction-presentation normalization of the fixed calculi and the augmented-presentation predicate. Localization of $f$ agrees with $r$ under these comparisons, before evaluation. In each finite degree its composite with extension evaluation and $\kappa_C$ equals $\kappa_D$ followed by the specified ordinary tensor comparison.

Define a completed open reduction comparison datum to consist of $r$ as above, preservation of completeness by both $j_!$ and $j^*$, the analogous restriction isomorphism $s:j^*\operatorname{red}_U\cong\operatorname{red}_X P$, reconstruction isomorphisms $u_U,u_X$ whose forward maps are exactly the respective reduction/limit adjunction units, and realization isomorphisms $d:\operatorname{red}_U J\operatorname{lim}_X\cong j_!$ and $v:\operatorname{red}_X P\operatorname{lim}_U\cong j^*$. Here composition order in these displayed functor words is left-to-right. Require $d=\operatorname{lim}_X(r^{-1})u_X^{-1}$ and $v=\operatorname{lim}_U(s^{-1})u_U^{-1}$, and require reduction of $d$ followed by $r$ to be the reduction/limit counit. Require the system unit equation $\operatorname{red}_U(\eta)\,s\,P(r)=\eta_{\rm sys}$ and system counit equation $r\,J(s)\,\epsilon_{\rm sys}=\operatorname{red}_X(\epsilon)$. Finally require the realized unit word $u_U\,\operatorname{lim}_U(\eta_{\rm sys})\,\operatorname{lim}_U(P(r^{-1}))\,v$ to equal the ordinary derived open unit, the realized counit word $d^{-1}\,\operatorname{lim}_X(J(s))\,\operatorname{lim}_X(\epsilon_{\rm sys})\,u_X^{-1}$ to equal its counit, and the strict-model predicate for $r$. All objects in these equations are evaluated on the corresponding complete input or its indicated extended/restricted object. This defines data and predicates only; it asserts no existence of tensor or reduction comparisons.
